headline: Proximie has 100+ terabytes of operating theatre video and is now running a large NHS surgical AI evaluation, so the bottleneck shifts from collecting video to finding, labelling and validating the few clips that actually teach a model.
what_they_build: Proximie sells a cloud platform and low bandwidth OR hardware that records, streams and de-identifies surgery, plus an Intelligence Suite that applies computer vision to surgical video for throughput, workflow and training analytics. Buyers are hospital groups and NHS trusts (500+ facilities, 50 countries) and 40+ medical device companies who want procedure and product usage insight. The September 2026 AWS, Deloitte and NHS surgical AI evaluation is the commercial proof point they are now selling against.
inferred_pipeline: OR hardware captures multi source video (laparoscope/endoscope feed, room cameras) with on device computer vision used for privacy masking of faces and identifiers, per their hardware page
Streams and recordings land in cloud object storage, likely AWS given the announced AWS partnership, organised by facility, specialty and procedure (guess: metadata is case level, not frame level)
Clips are selected for AI work largely by clinical request or procedure type rather than by frame level quality or content search (guess, no evidence of a curation tool)
Phase, step, instrument and critical view labelling done by clinicians or an outsourced vendor, probably in a bespoke internal viewer or a generic video tool (guess)

Models for phase recognition, instrument detection and timing analytics trained and reported inside the Intelligence Suite; evaluation for the AWS/Deloitte/NHS study likely needs a defensible held out, clinician adjudicated ground truth set
Results surfaced as throughput and workflow dashboards to hospitals and to medtech partners

hypotheses.pain: A large multi party AI evaluation needs an auditable, clinician reviewed ground truth set across many procedures, and spreadsheet plus bespoke viewer workflows will not survive that scrutiny.
hypotheses.evidence: Sept 2026 launch: 'largest ever surgical AI evaluation with AWS, Deloitte, and the NHS'; site claims 25+ clinical journal publications.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Annotate gives native long video labelling with ontology versioning, annotate to review to complete workflows, sampled review and routing, so every frame label has a named reviewer and audit trail. Active then scores inter-reviewer disagreement and surfaces likely label errors before they reach the study report.

hypotheses.pain: Surgeon annotator time is the scarcest resource; labelling full length cases frame by frame when 90 percent of a procedure is redundant burns that time.
hypotheses.evidence: 100+ TB of video and 80k recorded views on the site, no ML or annotation job ads found, implying a small team leaning on clinicians.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Index registers video in their own AWS bucket (data does not move), computes embeddings and frame quality metrics, and lets them build Collections of unique, in focus, event dense segments. Our own test cut frames to label by 61 percent while keeping 95 percent of target instances.

hypotheses.pain: Instrument and phase models trained on a few specialties degrade on new hospitals, scopes and lighting, and there is no systematic way to see which slices fail.
hypotheses.evidence: 500+ facilities, 50 countries, 40+ medtech partners implies heavy site and device variation; Intelligence Suite is sold on real-time CV.
hypotheses.encord_answer: Active imports their predictions and reports mAP/F1, PR curves and confusion matrix sliced by class, IoU threshold and any data metric such as brightness or sharpness, then correlates failure to data metrics so they know which cases to label next.

ontology.name: Surgical phase / step
ontology.why: Core timing and throughput signal; phases are temporal spans, not objects.

ontology.name: Instrument tip and shaft
ontology.why: Captures tool trajectory and economy of motion better than a box.

ontology.name: Instrument instance
ontology.why: Fast, trackable across video for tool presence, counts and usage analytics.

ontology.name: Anatomy / target organ
ontology.why: Irregular soft tissue boundaries; SAM 3 auto-segmentation suits this well.

ontology.name: Critical view / safety landmark
ontology.why: Clinically defined region used in quality and training scoring.

ontology.name: Implant or device under evaluation
ontology.why: Medtech partners pay for product usage and adoption evidence.

ontology.name: Bleeding or adverse event
ontology.why: Rare event flag for retrieval and for safety reporting in the NHS study.

ontology.name: Out of body / privacy risk frame
ontology.why: Scope out of body frames must be excluded before any human review.

case_study.name: Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital
case_study.why_it_matches: Clinician annotators, PHI sensitive imaging, academic grade ground truth for publication, which mirrors Proximie's NHS and journal publication posture.
case_study.numbers: Annotation time reduced from days to minutes on medical imaging; Encord holds SOC2 Type II, HIPAA and GDPR, with data staying in the customer's own bucket.

proof_of_value: Week 1, day 1-2: register one de-identified procedure cohort (say 200 laparoscopic cases) from their existing AWS bucket into Index. Nothing moves. Success: embeddings and quality metrics computed, out of body and degraded frames auto-flagged.

Week 1, day 3-5: build Collections by similarity and uniqueness, then compare a curated frame set against a random set of equal size. Success metric: at least 50 percent fewer frames to label while retaining 95 percent of instrument and phase events.

Week 2, day 1-3: stand up the phase plus instrument ontology in Annotate with an annotate to review to complete workflow, sampled clinician review and SAM 3 plus object tracking on a 20 case pilot. Success: median minutes of surgeon time per case, versus their current baseline.
Week 2, day 4: run an Agents stage with their existing phase model as a pre-labeller on the same cases. Success: percentage of pre-labels accepted without edit.

Week 2, day 5: import their model predictions into Active, produce mAP/F1 by class and confusion matrix sliced by hospital, scope and brightness. Success: a ranked list of the next 500 clips to label, plus a count of label errors found in their existing ground truth.
discovery_questions: For the AWS, Deloitte and NHS evaluation, who creates the ground truth labels, and how do you currently evidence reviewer agreement and audit trail to the trusts?
How do you decide which of the 100+ terabytes to annotate today, by procedure type, by surgeon request, or by something at frame level?
What does a surgeon annotator actually see, an internal viewer, a vendor tool, or something like CVAT, and how many minutes per case does it take?
When a phase or instrument model underperforms at a new site, how do you currently find out which slices are failing and what to label next?
De-identification happens on the hardware, so what are the rules for where labelled frames can be stored and who can see them, and does data need to stay in your AWS account?
risks: They may have already built internal labelling tooling tied to their own player and privacy masking, making a swap feel like a step back.
AWS and Deloitte are in the frame for the flagship evaluation, so tooling may be bundled into that engagement (SageMaker Ground Truth, Deloitte managed labelling) before we get a hearing.
Patient data governance across NHS trusts and 50 countries can stretch procurement and information governance review well beyond a normal cycle, even with SOC2 Type II and HIPAA.
Thin evidence on their actual ML team: no ML or CV job ads found, so AI may be a partner-delivered capability rather than an in-house build with budget.
opener_email:
